title: land runs selfdoc stale over the range before the stress run
goal: backlog.py land runs selfdoc.py stale --since <integration main> over the rebased range right after the rebase, before stress_test.py, the lookup eval and the lint, and stops at a step named stale, so a missing Self-Reviewed trailer fails in seconds; a stacked item whose lower item has landed loses that item's Self-Reviewed coverage and is caught the same way. Answers SP-5cwekumc's retrospective: six lands reached sync's stale gate only after a five-minute stress run (ST-g3w7v3el, ST-vfct2532 and four stacked branches).
notes: Merged findings, all clauses of the worker brief template: (1) Self-Reviewed goes inside the last trailer paragraph with KB-Work last, in the order Co-Authored-By, Session, Self-Reviewed, KB-Work, since git reads trailers from the last paragraph only (a lost full land rerun of about 25 minutes, three stale-gate stops); (2) the worker runs the stale pre-check on the rebased branch and reads every doc it lists, because the list mixes other sessions' changes with its own diff, and never runs done itself; (3) checks and tests run in the foreground with a timeout, never waiting for a background completion notice (workers stalled with staged changes and no commit), and a background land uses a timeout of 7200000 ms (one queued on the host lock was killed at 30 minutes); (4) the worker adds -k leaks whenever it adds or changes a test or fixture file (a new test file's literal failed the leak scan, one lost land). A test fails when the kb-worker definition lacks a clause.
